name: Wolfpine Village Starter Kit
purpose: Canonical reusable starter asset list for BG2/Pillars-like Wolfpine settlement scenes.

source_policy.notes: Generated full-scene art may be used for concept reference or selective salvage, but canonical kit pieces should usually be generated or prepared as isolated assets.

global_acceptance_checks: Painted or pre-rendered look, not pixel art.
Muted natural Wolfpine palette with readable warm daylight.
No text or UI baked into the asset.
Source and license/generation notes are recorded before production use.

placement_rules: Must face a walkable path or square.
Must include one clearly visible ground-level door.
Door approach must remain free of blocking props.
Can include warm window light, but not horror lighting.
acceptance_checks: Ground-level door is readable.
Windows cannot be mistaken for doors.
Roof and foundation are structurally believable.
Facade can be reused in more than one village scene.

placement_rules: Must face a walkable path or work yard.
Forge clutter must sit beside the door, not in front of it.
Chimney and work area should identify the building without labels.
acceptance_checks: Ground-level door is visible and reachable.
Forge identity is clear at game scale.
No stairs or platforms lead to invalid windows.

placement_rules: Should read as practical storage rather than noble housing.
Visible main door required even if locked in gameplay.
May include stacked sacks/crates only if they do not block the door.
acceptance_checks: Door exists and makes architectural sense.
Building reads as a storehouse from silhouette and props.
No critical access hidden by clutter.

placement_rules: Place in or near a village square clearing.
Keep actor approach space on at least two sides.
Do not make the roof/crossbeam so large it becomes an occluder.
acceptance_checks: Readable as a well at game scale.
Has usable contact shadow.
Can act as a hotspot focal object.

placement_rules: Place along the edge of a path, never across the only route.
Must leave a readable customer-facing side.
Awning may be an occluder only if it does not hide hotspots.
acceptance_checks: Stall direction is clear.
Produce/clutter reads without becoming visual noise.
Footprint is easy to block in collision.

placement_rules: Place near a wall, square, or crossroads.
Do not include readable real text; use marks and parchment shapes only.
Must have clear interaction side.
acceptance_checks: Reads as a notice board without legible text.
Not confused with a door or signpost.
Good hotspot silhouette.

placement_rules: Use only at ground level unless explicit stairs/platform exist.
Must visually connect to a walkable threshold.
Should support inn/storehouse use.
acceptance_checks: Reads as a door, not a window.
Has believable hinges/latch.
Perspective matches building facades.

placement_rules: Must be smaller than doors.
Do not place at ground level in a way that reads as an entrance.
Can be lit warm but should not dominate the facade.
acceptance_checks: Clearly reads as a window.
Does not imply player access.
Matches Wolfpine timber/plaster style.

placement_rules: Use to frame paths, not block required routes.
Can be repeated with small variation and decals.
Should have collision if placed across movement.
acceptance_checks: Repeats without obvious seams.
Perspective matches ground plane.
Not too visually heavy for path edges.

placement_rules: Place beside buildings or forge work areas.
Do not block doors or hotspot approach arcs.
Can be combined with crates/barrels for clutter clusters.
acceptance_checks: Reads as woodpile at small scale.
Has a grounded contact shadow.
Works beside both cottage and blacksmith facades.

placement_rules: Use in small groups or beside buildings.
Do not place directly over important doors/hotspots.
Can be mirrored/varied with decals.
acceptance_checks: Readable round form in pseudo-isometric view.
Does not look like a modern object.
Small enough for repeated dressing.

placement_rules: Use near storehouse, stall, or inn service side.
Can stack in small groups if silhouette stays readable.
Do not block required paths.
acceptance_checks: Perspective matches the ground plane.
Edges are readable but not pixel-sharp.
Works with barrel/sack clutter.

placement_rules: Use to soften road, wall, and path edges.
Should not imply collision unless used densely.
Palette should be natural green, not neon.
acceptance_checks: Blends with mud/cobble edges.
Not too contrasty at game scale.
Can repeat without obvious pattern.

placement_rules: Use to blend roads and village square edges.
Must not obscure walkability readability.
Prefer transparent decal-like treatment.
acceptance_checks: Works over cobble, dirt, and road bases.
Does not look like a hard-edged sticker.
Supports path direction visually.

placement_rules: Use only on foreground layer.
Never hide doors, exits, or required hotspots.
Can frame the scene edges and add depth.
acceptance_checks: Looks like a foreground element, not a ground prop.
Soft enough to avoid distracting from gameplay.
Does not cover important interaction points.
